newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin worried about tensions in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin worried about tensions in Belarus.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday joined a growing international chorus of concern over a fierce power struggle in Belarus that has pitted hardline leader Alexander Lukashenko against parliament and other institutions.

Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin, recovering from heart surgery at a clinic outside Moscow, had discussed Belarus at a 90-minute meeting with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

"The president and the prime minister expressed alarm about rising tension in Belarus society and the hope that common sense and the art of political compromise will replace the ambitions and confrontations among politicians," he said.
Russia joined Belarus in a two-state "community" last April. Lukashenko, whom opponents accuse of trying to set up a dictatorship, wants to forge even closer ties with Moscow.
"It is natural that Russia take an objective interest in the stability and prosperity of a brotherly state that is very close to us," Yastrzhembsky said.

Russian foreign ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin, speaking at a regular news briefing, also called on the two sides in Minsk to resolve their differences "within the framework of peaceful dialogue and not by way of accusations and threats".

Parliamentary deputies, who have been occupying the chamber round the clock since Friday, have started impeachment proceedings against Lukashenko but the president, who controls the security forces, appears unfazed by the move.
He hopes to boost his powers and extend his mandate by more than two years in a referendum that ends on Sunday.
The United States and other governments have expressed concern at events in the country sandwiched between Russia and Poland.

The most outspoken criticism has come from leading German parliamentarian Karsten Voigt, president of the North Atlantic Assembly, who said Lukashenko's behaviour was "illegal, non-democratic and sometimes even crazy".
